evidence: store.py:110-112 submits functools.partial(func,...) to a ThreadPoolExecutor and awaits asyncio.wrap_future(future). In CPython (>=3.11, pyproject requires-python), wrap_future chains via _chain_future/_copy_future_state, which calls dest.set_exception(_convert_future_exc(source.exception())). _convert_future_exc only maps concurrent.futures.CancelledError/TimeoutError/InvalidStateError to asyncio equivalents (TimeoutError is the builtin alias in 3.11+); all other exceptions, including MemoryNotFoundError, MemoryCorruptionError, MemoryInputError, MemoryChangedError and generic Exception, are the same object with type and attributes preserved. Awaiting then re-raises that object. server.py handlers' except clauses (553 MemoryInputError/MemoryChangedError, 571 MemoryNotFoundError, 598 MemoryNotFoundError, 702 MemoryCorruptionError, plus broad except Exception at 555/575/603/627/710/734) wrap the await run_memory_call, so they see the same exception as before. Verified from CPython knowledge of asyncio.futures, not by reading the stdlib source in this environment. Rejection line about nested calls is unrelated to this claim.

store.py:110-116 submits to the single-worker executor, awaits asyncio.wrap_future(future), and on CancelledError attaches functools.partial(_log_call_after_cancel, name) before re-raising. Per CPython semantics (asyncio.futures._chain_future._call_check_cancel calls source.cancel() when the destination asyncio future is cancelled; concurrent.futures.Future.cancel succeeds only for PENDING and returns False for RUNNING; add_done_callback invokes the callback immediately in the caller thread if the future is already done), a queued call is cancelled and never runs. _log_call_after_cancel (store.py:87-96) returns on future.cancelled(), logs INFO on success, and WARNING with exc_info on failure, so each outcome is handled. Verified from the implementation in the head view; CPython behavior is from my knowledge of the stdlib, not re-read from the stdlib source. The rejection line (nested-call deadlock) is unrelated to this claim.

store.py:87-96: returns silently if future.cancelled(); logger.info naming `name` when exception() is None; otherwise logger.warning(..., name, exc_info=exc) with exc a BaseException instance. Python's logging.Logger._log (stdlib) converts an exception-instance exc_info to (type, value, __traceback__), so the traceback is rendered. future.exception() is safe since the future is done and not cancelled when the done-callback runs.

store.py:75-84 _get_executor lazily creates one process-wide ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) under a lock, so every run_memory_call (store.py:110) from any thread or event loop submits to the same single-worker executor. ThreadPoolExecutor.submit puts work items on a FIFO SimpleQueue, and one worker takes them one at a time, so execution is serial and in submission order. submit is called synchronously before the first await, so submission order is the call order. Hostile input traced: two submissions from different loops (CLI asyncio.run loop and a server loop) both reach the same executor, still serialized. A cancelled caller before start has its future cancelled and the item is dropped, which the docstring states. A started call runs to completion, so later calls wait. An exception in a work item does not kill the worker thread. The recorded rejection concerns nested calls, which the docstring already warns about and which would block rather than overlap, so it does not affect this claim.

store.py:83 builds ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as the process-wide singleton (_get_executor, 75-84). run_memory_call (110-112) submits to that executor and awaits wrap_future. Input traced: func submitted via run_memory_call runs on the sqllens-memory thread and calls asyncio.run(run_memory_call(g)). The inner call does _get_executor().submit(g): same singleton, its only worker is occupied by the outer func, which is blocked inside asyncio.run waiting for the inner future. g is queued behind it and never starts, so the inner future never resolves and the outer func never returns. This is a deadlock. A fresh event loop does not help, because the executor is module-level and shared. Nothing in the code can interrupt the wait: there is no timeout or reentrancy check. The rejection line (callers are server.py handlers and importer.import_bundle, none nested) is consistent with this. It concerns whether a guard is needed, not whether the docstring is true.

store.py:75-84 single-worker ThreadPoolExecutor (max_workers=1), so later submissions queue behind a running call. store.py:110-116: run_memory_call submits, awaits asyncio.wrap_future(future); on CancelledError the asyncio future's cancellation is propagated by _chain_future to the concurrent Future.cancel(), which succeeds only while the work item is still pending; the executor worker then skips it (set_running_or_notify_cancel false), so a queued cancelled call never runs. If the call already started, cancel() returns False and the worker runs func to completion; the one worker blocks later calls regardless of the handler's asyncio locks being released (these are separate from the executor). The except branch adds _log_call_after_cancel (87-96): returns if cancelled, logs logger.info naming the function (__qualname__) on success, logger.warning with exc_info=exc on failure; add_done_callback fires immediately if already done. Absolute-claim input: cancel arriving just as the worker picks up the item -> cancel() returns False, call counts as started and runs to completion, logged by the callback; consistent with the claim. store.py:83 builds the memory worker as a plain ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix='sqllens-memory') with no daemon option.
